**10. POST-FESTIVAL WRAP-UP AND REVIEW**

**10.1 Overview**

The Merlion Sounds Festival 2026 was held over the weekend of 8–9 August 2026 at the Marina Bay Promenade site. This section consolidates the post-festival wrap-up, including the debrief summaries, vendor evaluations, and lessons learned for future events. The wrap-up process was coordinated by the Festival Director's Office, with input from all section heads, the Control Room, and the Vendor Liaison Officer.

The post-festival review period ran from 10 August 2026 to 20 August 2026. All section heads were required to submit their debrief reports by 14 August 2026. A consolidated debrief meeting was held on 17 August 2026 at the Lumina Events office. This section reflects the outcomes of that meeting and the submitted reports.

**10.2 Debrief Summary – Key Findings**

The following table summarises the key findings from the debrief reports. The findings are grouped by operational area and include the status of each item as of 20 August 2026.

| Ref | Operational Area | Finding | Status (as of 20 Aug 2026) |
|-----|------------------|---------|-----------------------------|
| DB-01 | Crowd Management | The east entrance queue exceeded the planned capacity during the peak period on 8 August. Additional barriers were deployed at 1930 hrs. | Resolved – no further incidents |
| DB-02 | Sound System | A brief audio dropout was reported on the main stage at 2115 hrs on 8 August. The Technical Director traced it to a loose cable connection. | Resolved – cable replaced |
| DB-03 | Vendor Operations | Two food vendors reported low water pressure at their stalls on the morning of 9 August. The issue was traced to a blocked filter at the main supply point. | Resolved – filter cleaned |
| DB-04 | Medical | A total of 14 first-aid cases were recorded across the weekend. None required hospitalisation. | Closed |
| DB-05 | Waste Management | Waste collection points were observed to be at capacity by 2200 hrs on both nights. Additional collections were scheduled. | Resolved – additional collection runs added |
| DB-06 | Staff Welfare | Staff rest area was reported as insufficiently shaded during the afternoon of 8 August. Additional shade sails were installed by 1500 hrs. | Resolved |

**10.3 Debrief Meeting Minutes – 17 August 2026**

The consolidated debrief meeting was held on 17 August 2026 at the Lumina Events office, commencing at 1000 hrs. The meeting was chaired by the Festival Director. Attendance included all section heads, the Technical Director, the Vendor Liaison Officer, and the Safety Officer.

Key discussion points:

- **Crowd flow**: The Crowd Management Coordinator noted that the east entrance bottleneck was primarily due to a higher-than-expected number of attendees arriving between 1830 and 1930 hrs. The queue management plan (Attachment C-2, revision 2) was followed, but the rate of arrival exceeded the modelled figure. It was agreed that future editions should model arrival rates using data from the ticket sales platform, which showed a 12% higher peak-hour arrival than the previous year.

- **Audio dropout**: The Technical Director explained that the audio dropout on the main stage was caused by a loose Speakon connector on the monitor line. The fault was identified and rectified within 12 minutes. The equipment fault log form was completed and filed. A recommendation was made to include a pre-show check of all Speakon connections in the daily technical checklist.

5.1 The organiser must appoint a Crowd Management Coordinator (CMC) who is present on site for the duration of the event.

5.4 Barriers and fencing must be installed as per the approved site plan. No barrier may be removed, relocated, or left unsecured during the event.

5.5 In the event of an evacuation order, the CMC shall direct the audience to the nearest assembly point. Assembly points are marked on the Site Plan (Appendix A) and on signage around the Venue.

**10. POST-FESTIVAL WRAP-UP AND REVIEW**

**10.1 Overview**

The Merlion Sounds Festival 2026 was held over the weekend of 8–9 August 2026 at the Marina Bay Promenade site. This section consolidates the post-festival wrap-up, including the debrief summaries, vendor evaluations, and lessons learned for future events. The wrap-up process was coordinated by the Festival Director's Office, with input from all section heads, the Control Room, and the Vendor Liaison Officer.

The post-festival review period ran from 10 August 2026 to 20 August 2026. All section heads were required to submit their debrief reports by 14 August 2026. A consolidated debrief meeting was held on 17 August 2026 at the Lumina Events office. This section reflects the outcomes of that meeting and the submitted reports.

**10.2 Debrief Summary – Key Findings**

The following table summarises the key findings from the debrief reports. The findings are grouped by operational area and include the status of each item as of 20 August 2026.

| Ref | Operational Area | Finding | Status (as of 20 Aug 2026) |
|-----|------------------|---------|-----------------------------|
| DB-01 | Crowd Management | The east entrance queue exceeded the planned capacity during the peak period on 8 August. Additional barriers were deployed at 1930 hrs. | Resolved – no further incidents |
| DB-02 | Sound System | A brief audio dropout was reported on the main stage at 2115 hrs on 8 August. The Technical Director traced it to a loose cable connection. | Resolved – cable replaced |
| DB-03 | Vendor Operations | Two food vendors reported low water pressure at their stalls on the morning of 9 August. The issue was traced to a blocked filter at the main supply point. | Resolved – filter cleaned |
| DB-04 | Medical | A total of 14 first-aid cases were recorded across the weekend. None required hospitalisation. | Closed |
| DB-05 | Waste Management | Waste collection points were observed to be at capacity by 2200 hrs on both nights. Additional collections were scheduled. | Resolved – additional collection runs added |
| DB-06 | Staff Welfare | Staff rest area was reported as insufficiently shaded during the afternoon of 8 August. Additional shade sails were installed by 1500 hrs. | Resolved |

**10.3 Debrief Meeting Minutes – 17 August 2026**

The consolidated debrief meeting was held on 17 August 2026 at the Lumina Events office, commencing at 1000 hrs. The meeting was chaired by the Festival Director. Attendance included all section heads, the Technical Director, the Vendor Liaison Officer, and the Safety Officer.

Key discussion points:

- **Crowd flow**: The Crowd Management Coordinator noted that the east entrance bottleneck was primarily due to a higher-than-expected number of attendees arriving between 1830 and 1930 hrs. The queue management plan (Attachment C-2, revision 2) was followed, but the rate of arrival exceeded the modelled figure. It was agreed that future editions should model arrival rates using data from the ticket sales platform, which showed a 12% higher peak-hour arrival than the previous year.

- **Audio dropout**: The Technical Director explained that the audio dropout on the main stage was caused by a loose Speakon connector on the monitor line. The fault was identified and rectified within 12 minutes. The equipment fault log form was completed and filed. A recommendation was made to include a pre-show check of all Speakon connections in the daily technical checklist.

**16 Aug 2026 (Sun) – 22:40**

Technician: S. Raj (on-call standby)

Work: Emergency callout – PDU-2. Stage power fault reported during setup for Marina Bay Fringe Festival (event scheduled 19–22 Aug).

Sequence of events (from memory, verified against panel log afterwards):

- 21:58 – Stage crew reported "half the lights went dead" on the east stage. FOH engineer called standby line.
- 22:05 – Arrived on site. Panel meter on PDU-2 showed no alarms, but branch circuit B3 was in TRIPPED position. Breaker handle mid-travel.
- 22:12 – Attempted re-close once. Breaker tripped again immediately. No visible arc or burn marks on enclosure.
- 22:20 – Isolated B3 by switching breaker to OFF and padlocking the enclosure door. Tagged out with LOTO tag #8841.
- 22:25 – Advised stage manager to re-route affected loads to PDU-1 via available spare circuits (2 x 32A). Crew confirmed this was acceptable for the night.
- 22:40 – Completed initial report. Left site. No further calls overnight.

Remarks: This is the same breaker (PDU-2-B3) identified on 16 Jul 2026 as having contact resistance above spec (0.48 mΩ vs 0.35 mΩ limit). Replacement part was ordered 16 Jul with ETA 19 Aug. This incident is consistent with the earlier finding. Breaker to be replaced before any further use.

---

**17 Aug 2026 (Mon) – 09:15**

Technician: D. Lim

Work: Site visit – PDU-2. Verify tag-out condition and prepare for breaker replacement.

Result:

- LOTO tag #8841 in place. Enclosure padlocked. Breaker handle confirmed OFF.
- Panel log indicates B3 has not been re-energised since 22:20 on 16 Aug.
- Visual inspection of breaker face and terminals: no discolouration, no smell of burnt insulation. Terminals on load side checked with torque wrench – all fasteners at spec.
- Measured insulation resistance phase-to-phase and phase-to-earth on the load cable (de-energised): 850 MΩ, 920 MΩ, 1.1 GΩ. Acceptable.

Remarks: Replacement breaker not yet delivered. Supplier (Chuan Lee Electrical) confirmed ETA 19 Aug, delivery to our workshop. Will install on receipt.

Work: Update – breaker PDU-2-B3 replacement status.

Result: Called Chuan Lee Electrical at 10:45. Part (MCCB 250A, 3-pole, 36 kA) is in transit from distributor. ETA remains 19 Aug, but they could not confirm AM/PM delivery. Left message for their sales rep to call back with tracking number.

Remarks: If part arrives after 14:00 on 19 Aug, installation will be done on 20 Aug morning. Festival opening is 19 Aug evening – B3 will remain isolated for the first night. Stage crew already rerouted, no impact expected.

---

**19 Aug 2026 (Wed) – 15:40**

Technician: D. Lim

Work: Breaker PDU-2-B3 replacement – part received.

Result:

- Part delivered to workshop at 14:10. Verified model and rating against purchase order #PO-26231: MCCB 250A, 3-pole, 36 kA breaking capacity. Matches.

- Re-energised B3 at 15:25. No alarms. Panel meter normal.
- Load test: connected the east stage lighting circuits that had been rerouted. Breaker held under load for 10 minutes. No trip, no heat.

4. LOAD-IN PROCEDURES

4.1 Load-in is permitted only during the hours stated on the event permit. Standard load-in hours are 07:00 to 22:00. Extended load-in hours (up to 06:00 the next day) may be approved for large-scale productions, subject to a noise assessment.

4.2 All vehicles entering the Venue must use the Production Compound gate (Gate B, off Bayfront Avenue). Vehicles must not exceed 5 km/h within the compound.

4.3 Forklifts and boom lifts may only be operated by certified personnel. The organiser must submit the relevant certification documents to the Venue Management Branch at least 48 hours before load-in.

4.4 The organiser shall provide a minimum of two (2) safety marshals during any crane or elevated work. Marshals must wear high-visibility vests.

4.5 All load-in activities must cease at least 30 minutes before the scheduled start of the event, to allow for a safety sweep of the stage and audience areas.

---

5. CAPACITY AND CROWD MANAGEMENT

5.1 The organiser must appoint a Crowd Management Coordinator (CMC) who is present on site for the duration of the event.

5.2 The CMC shall ensure that the audience count in each zone does not exceed the limits in Section 3.1. Counting shall be done using a combination of ticket scans, manual clickers at entry points, and CCTV review.

5.4 Barriers and fencing must be installed as per the approved site plan. No barrier may be removed, relocated, or left unsecured during the event.

5.5 In the event of an evacuation order, the CMC shall direct the audience to the nearest assembly point. Assembly points are marked on the Site Plan (Appendix A) and on signage around the Venue.

5.6 The organiser shall provide a public address (PA) system capable of covering all audience zones. The PA system must be tested at least once on the morning of the show day.

---

6. SOUND AND NOISE REGULATIONS

6.1 The Venue operates under a set of sound level limits designed to balance event experience with the amenity of nearby residents and the surrounding Gardens.

6.2 The following table lists the maximum permissible sound levels at the mixing console position (FOH) for each performance area. These are "slow response" readings, A-weighted, measured over a continuous 15-minute period.

---

**7. NOISE REGULATIONS (CONTINUED)**

7.1 The following table lists the maximum permissible sound levels at the mixing console position (FOH) for each performance area. These are "slow response" readings, A-weighted, measured over a continuous 15-minute period.

| Area | Max Sound Level (dBA) | Remarks |
|------|------------------------|---------|
| Main Stage | 95 dBA | Current controlled limit for all ticketed events. |
| Meadow (North) | 85 dBA | For acoustic sets, DJ sets, and secondary stages. |
| The Crescent | 80 dBA | Family-friendly programming only. |
| Bayfront Plaza (East) | 88 dBA | Limited to 3 events per calendar month. |

7.2 Sound level monitoring shall be conducted by the Venue's appointed acoustic consultant. Readings are taken at the FOH position and at a reference point 50 m from the nearest residential block along Marina Gardens Drive.

7.3 If the measured level exceeds the applicable limit for more than 15 continuous minutes, the Venue may issue a written warning. A second warning within the same event will result in a reduction of the permitted level by 3 dBA for the remainder of the show.

7.4 All amplified sound must cease by 22:30 hours on weekdays and by 23:00 hours on weekends and public holidays. This includes sound checks and rehearsals.

7.5 The organiser shall provide a contactable person to respond to noise complaints during the event. The Venue will route complaints received via the NEA hotline or the Gardens' security desk to this person within 15 minutes.

---

**8. EVACUATION AND EMERGENCY PROCEDURES**

8.1 In the event of an emergency requiring evacuation, the Venue's Emergency Response Team (ERT) will activate the alarm system. The organiser's staff must follow the instructions of the ERT and assist in directing the audience to assembly points.

8.2 Assembly points are designated as follows:

| Assembly Point | Location | Capacity |
|----------------|----------|----------|
| AP-1 | Meadow Lawn (North) | 3,000 pax |
| AP-2 | Bayfront Plaza (East) | 2,500 pax |
| AP-3 | Kingfisher Walk (South) | 1,500 pax |

8.3 The organiser shall brief all event staff and volunteers on evacuation routes and assembly points during the pre-show briefing. A record of attendance for this briefing must be kept and made available to the Venue upon request.

8.4 Emergency exits and evacuation routes must be kept clear at all times. No equipment, staging, or storage may be placed within 3 m of any exit door or marked evacuation path.

8.5 In the event of lightning within a 5 km radius of the Venue, all outdoor activities must cease immediately. The organiser shall have a lightning monitoring service in place and shall designate a person to issue the "all clear" signal.

8.6 The Venue maintains a first aid room located at the Administration Block, next to the loading dock. The organiser shall provide at least one certified first aider on site during all event hours.

---

**9. LOAD-IN AND LOAD-OUT PROCEDURES**

9.1 Load-in access to the Venue is via the loading dock located at the south-east corner of the Bayfront Plaza. Access hours are from 06:00 to 22:00 daily, unless prior arrangement has been made with the Venue Operations Team.

9.2 Vehicles entering the loading dock must not exceed 3.5 m in height and 12 m in length. Oversized vehicles require a separate permit and must be accompanied by a Venue escort.
